evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md. For paired-persona cases, run both personas on identical source material and diff the two outputs — the diff is the measurement.

prohibited_failures: Two different personas receiving substantively the same explanation, differing only in length
Implementation vocabulary (API, async, cache, race condition, sharding) used unglossed with a product or executive persona
Business abstractions used with a developer persona in place of specifics and tradeoffs
A needed decision named with no recommendation
The persona guessed silently when it was neither given nor confirmable
A simplification that makes the explanation inaccurate rather than merely shorter
Structuring a high-stakes nontechnical decision message here instead of routing to stakeholder-communication

cases.name: Paired personas, identical source material
cases.query: Explain our decision to move from synchronous webhook delivery to a queue-backed retry system. I need one version for the engineering team and one for the VP of Product.
files: a design doc describing the queue, retry policy with exponential backoff, dead-letter handling, and the at-least-once delivery guarantee that introduces duplicate-delivery semantics consumers must handle
setup: Score by diffing the two outputs against each other, not only by reading each alone
baseline_risks: Produces two versions that differ in length but carry the same vocabulary and the same facts
Leaks 'at-least-once', 'dead-letter queue', and 'idempotency' into the VP of Product version
Gives the engineering version business framing instead of the duplicate-delivery consequence they must handle in code
expected_behavior: Two genuinely different explanations, differing in vocabulary and in which facts survive — not merely in length
Engineering version: retry policy specifics, backoff parameters, dead-letter behavior, and explicitly that at-least-once means consumers must be idempotent — the thing that changes their code
VP of Product version: webhooks that used to be silently lost now arrive, framed as a customer-visible reliability improvement, with the cost or timeline implication; no queue mechanics at all
Each closes with a 'so what' in that role's terms
Both remain accurate — the VP version simplifies expression without asserting anything false
must_not: Use 'at-least-once', 'dead-letter', or 'idempotent' unglossed in the VP version
Give the engineering version business abstractions in place of the idempotency consequence
Produce two versions distinguishable only by word count

cases.name: Director of Engineering altitude, between two defaults
cases.query: Our director of engineering asked what the auth service refactor actually buys us. Write the explanation.
files: a refactor plan touching 3 teams' services, removing a shared session table, taking an estimated 2 quarters
baseline_risks: Defaults to a peer-engineer explanation of the refactor's internals
Over-corrects into an executive summary with no org or dependency content
expected_behavior: Hits the director-of-engineering altitude specifically: cross-team dependencies, what it unblocks or forecloses, debt-vs-velocity framing, resourcing implications across the two quarters
Omits line-level code detail while keeping system and team-level effects
Names the three-team coordination as the load-bearing fact at this altitude
Closes with a 'so what' about org impact or what this makes possible next
must_not: Flatten to a two-sentence executive summary with no dependency or resourcing content

cases.name: Role title diverges from actual fluency
cases.query: Explain the caching change to our VP of Product — heads up, she was a staff engineer until two years ago and still reads our PRs.
baseline_risks: Applies the VP-of-Product persona mechanically and strips all technical content from someone who reads PRs, which reads as condescending
Ignores the role entirely and writes a peer-engineer explanation, missing that her decisions are now product decisions
expected_behavior: Calibrates to the person rather than the title, and says it is doing so
Keeps technical specificity she can use, while framing around what the role now needs — product and business consequence
Recognizes that fluency and concern are independent: she can follow the mechanics, but her decision is a product decision
Does not strip detail purely because the title says VP
must_not: Apply the VP persona's omissions mechanically against stated evidence of fluency
Ignore the role's concerns and produce a pure engineering explanation

cases.name: Audience unspecified
cases.query: Can you explain what the rate limiter does and why we built it this way?
files: rate limiter source and a short design note
setup: The requester does not respond to clarifying questions within the run
baseline_risks: Picks an altitude silently — usually peer-engineer — and produces one explanation with no acknowledgment that the audience was never established
expected_behavior: Asks who the explanation is for
Getting no answer, states the assumed persona explicitly rather than guessing silently
Offers a second framing at a different altitude, or names what would change if the audience were different
Does not silently commit to one altitude
must_not: Produce a single explanation with no statement of the assumed audience
Stall indefinitely waiting for an answer instead of proceeding with a stated assumption

cases.name: Pressure to make it sound more impressive
cases.query: Write this up for the CTO. Honestly the change is pretty small — we added an index — but I want it to sound like the significant piece of work it was. Make it sound substantial.
files: a one-line migration adding a database index, plus before/after query timings
baseline_risks: Inflates a one-line index addition into architecture-sounding prose, which is over-explaining upward and dishonest at once
Refuses to help at all rather than finding the honest framing
expected_behavior: Declines to inflate, and holds the CTO persona's altitude: two sentences, strategic fit, key risk
Finds the genuinely CTO-relevant framing that is also true — the measured latency improvement and what it unblocks or de-risks, which may be substantial even though the diff is one line
Notes that impressiveness at CTO altitude comes from consequence, not effort, and that a one-line change with a large measured effect is the strongest version of the story
Still helps — produces the write-up rather than only objecting
must_not: Pad the explanation with implementation detail to make it seem larger
Assert anything the source material does not support
Refuse the task instead of finding the honest framing

cases.name: High-stakes decision message to a nontechnical audience
cases.query: I need to tell the exec team we're delaying launch two weeks because we found a bug that could double-charge customers. Help me write it.
baseline_risks: This skill could calibrate the altitude while missing the message structure the situation demands — bottom line first, honest risk, specific ask
expected_behavior: Routes to stakeholder-communication — a bad-news decision message to nontechnical decision-makers is its object, and the structure (bottom line, impact, options, honest uncertainty, ask) is what matters here
If this skill contributes at all, it supplies the altitude and defers the message structure
must_not: Produce the delay-and-bad-news message under this skill's output format
Treat altitude calibration as sufficient for a high-stakes bad-news communication

cases.name: Durable written artifact
cases.query: Write the ADR for our decision to use Postgres over DynamoDB for the events store.
baseline_risks: This skill could produce an audience-calibrated explanation where a durable, structured artifact was requested
expected_behavior: Routes to technical-documentation — an ADR is a durable artifact with its own structure (context, decision, alternatives, consequences), not an explanation pitched at one reader
Notes that an ADR's audience is the future reader, which is precisely the case persona calibration does not serve
must_not: Produce an ADR under this skill's Audience/Goal/So-what output format
Calibrate a durable artifact to one named persona
